quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x150, Mora x20000, Hero's Wit x3

dialogues.speaker: Bulletin Board
dialogues.text: "In the light of alternating day cycles, one can see the homeward figure of the lighthouse on the bridge."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What is this...? A riddle? Or a proverb or something...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Alternating day cycles? Homeward figure...

dialogues.speaker: Kamal
dialogues.text: Hello, traveler. Are you interested in Drusus's riddle too?

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: It was set up by an Akademiya researcher named Drusus.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: As far as I know, he's an eccentric even among the Akademiya crowd.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: He loves to talk about riddles with anyone, as well as research all kinds of encryption methods.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: But some of his riddles are too incomprehensible, so not many people are willing to deal with him.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: So he came up with the "solve riddles for prizes" idea.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: Simply put, this riddle actually hints at a treasure trove.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: You just have to show up at the right place at the right time using the right method and you'll get the treasure.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: Drusus also gave a hint, saying that the locations are all within Sumeru City.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: But as you can see, no adventurer has been able to succeed.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: You can certainly try if you're interested.

response.speaker: Kamal
response.text: But if you ask me, I'd tell you to do something else more productive...

choices.text: Do you know who set it up?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This really is the place. "The sole path to knowledge" are these bridges.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a note in here too... Is this chain of riddles still not over?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Let Paimon see. This says...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Brilliant colors are blooming, with watery pearls there lingering."

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Wh—What does it mean!?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon thinks it's describing some kind of flower, but what does "with watery pearls there lingering" mean...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So it really is talking about lotuses. Now that Paimon thinks about it... Those leaves do seem to hold "watery pearls"...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: There's a note here too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Please go to the front door of the Temple of Knowledge at noon."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This is quite direct. Paimon thought it was gonna be another riddle.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Whatever. Let's just do what this says and go to the front door of the Temple of Knowledge at noon.

dialogues.speaker: Riddle on the notice board
dialogues.text: "In the light of alternating day cycles, one can see the homeward figure of the lighthouse on the bridge."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "Noon, after eating breakfast, when daylight shifts with daylight."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So... this means "go to the top of the lighthouse at noon"!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon worked so hard! It's actually so easy!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Never mind, it's all good as long as the treasure is found... Let's see what's in the chest.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a note here too...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What does it say? Let Paimon see.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "A mirror not made of glass reflects every drama."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is this hinting at the next treasure location?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: It mentions "drama" so does it mean the treasure location has to do with "theater"?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't understand... But it feels like it's hinting at an amazing place.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "A mirror not made of glass reflects every drama."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Reflects every drama... So it meant this theater...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A mirror not made of glass... So it meant the pond behind the theater...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This place isn't amazing at all! Why use such an impressive riddle to describe such an ordinary place?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: There's a note in here too.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: A riddle again? Is this a serial riddle...?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: "The sole path to knowledge."

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: This looks... not that difficult...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: The only place that can represent knowledge in Sumeru City must be there...

dialogues.speaker: Drusus
dialogues.text: Is no one coming today either...?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Is this the "front door of the Temple of Knowledge"?

dialogues.speaker: Drusus
dialogues.text: That's right! This is the front door of the Temple of Knowledge. You seem to have solved all my riddles.

dialogues.speaker: Drusus
dialogues.text: And that's wonderful! I thought no one would be able to do that today either! Actually, I'm going back to have lunch soon...

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Why did you write these riddles?

dialogues.speaker: Drusus
dialogues.text: Because it's fun, of course.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That was a quick answer!

dialogues.speaker: Drusus
dialogues.text: Other than that reason, why do you think I wrote down these riddles?

dialogues.speaker: Drusus
dialogues.text: Did you think that I was just enjoying being difficult?

response.speaker: Drusus
response.text: Hahaha, then you have misunderstood me, like some people in the Akademiya.

response.speaker: Drusus
response.text: I wrote these riddles down because I simply enjoy the feeling of pondering that comes with puzzling them out.

response.speaker: Drusus
response.text: When you look back at my riddles, you can see that there is always a keyword leading to the final answer.

response.speaker: Drusus
response.text: If you use this keyword as a base and keep thinking about it, the final answer will gradually present itself.

response.speaker: Drusus
response.text: If I'd simply wanted to make things difficult for others, I would erase all the clues and turn the riddle into a truly unsolvable problem.

response.speaker: Drusus
response.text: Let's not talk about this now. Since you've solved all my riddles, you can take these.

response.speaker: Drusus
response.text: This is the reward you've won with your pondering. Keep them.
